topic_title: Understand the characteristics of basic univariate distributions and how to generate samples from them
cmp_edition: IFoA CS1 Core Reading / CMP · 2026 syllabus alignment

mission.display_title: Place continuous families beside discrete ones
mission.mission_purpose: Today's Mission exists to extend yesterday's discrete recognition into continuous univariate families. So you can characterise Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, and continuous uniform by support and typical use, without pretending probability evaluation is finished.
mission.tutor_intent: Today I will force the candidate to discriminate continuous families by support and modelling role, and to refuse treating 'everything is Normal' as a default without warrant. So continuous entry matches the same Sensei standard as discrete entry.
mission.educational_intent: Produce a cognitive move from 'continuous = Normal only' to 'I can place the syllabus continuous families by support and typical actuarial/statistical role, with one honest non-default.'
mission.learning_objective: Describe the characteristics of Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, and uniform continuous distributions on an interval, and match key members to recognisable modelling situations.
mission.concept_focus: Support / shape story → continuous family → refuse Normal-by-default theatre.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday you matched discrete counting situations to 2.1.1 families. Today the same 2.1 topic continues at 2.1.2: continuous univariate characteristics sit beside the discrete map. Not a new chapter leap.
mission.why_now: You've placed discrete families; today place continuous ones beside them so you don't default every continuous problem to Normal.
mission.expected_benefit: A continuous-family placement map with one refused Normal default. Study Progress for today's Session, not Topic Complete for 2.1.3–2.1.6.
mission.explainability: Assigned as Campaign Beta Day 3 because contiguous 2.1.1→2.1.2 completes lawful distributional entry without swallowing probability evaluation and generation LOs.
success_criteria: Closed-book, name the syllabus continuous families in LO 2.1.2.
For three modelling situations, choose a fitting continuous family with one characteristic warrant (support or shape role).
task_descriptions: Sketch continuous families grouped by support/role before opening the CMP.
Complete Guided Reading through CMP treatment of Syllabus 2.1.2 continuous distributions.
Closed-book: place families and refuse one Normal default.

session.session_educational_purpose: This Session exists to execute today's Mission: build and stress-test continuous family placement. Not to complete 2.1.3 probability/quantile drills or random-variable generation.
session.session_tutor_purpose: In this hour I will set focus questions on continuous family characteristics, exit for CMP work on 2.1.2, then retrieve place–warrant–refuse-Normal-default. So continuous entry stays judgement.
session.wrap_up: Session complete for Place continuous families beside discrete ones. You practised selective CMP reading on Syllabus 2.1.2 and stress-tested continuous family placement. This is Study Progress for today's block. Not Topic Complete for probability evaluation (2.1.3), Poisson process (2.1.4), or generation methods (2.1.5–2.1.6). Tomorrow is Revision mode.
session.confidence_prompt: How confident are you that you could place three continuous families and refuse a Normal default closed-book tomorrow morning? Rate 1–5 and give one honest warrant.

reading_guidance.lead_line: Purpose of this reading: use the CMP to extract support and typical modelling role for each continuous family in Syllabus 2.1.2. So continuous choice is support-led. Extract that catalogue frame from the CMP, then stop before probability/quantile evaluation beyond today's block.
focus_questions: What support does each continuous family typically live on?
When is lognormal or gamma a better claim-size story than Normal?
What roles do t, F, and chi-square often play relative to Normal sampling theory?
You will later place families and refuse one Normal-by-default misuse.
misconception_watch: Watch for Normal-by-default on strictly positive skewed quantities.
Watch for confusing the roster with full quantile calculation skill.
Watch for beginning 2.1.3 drills inside this sitting.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: continuous family roster
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Name the continuous distribution families in Syllabus 2.1.2. For Normal, lognormal, exponential, and gamma, give one short modelling or support cue each.
knowledge_checks.body: Roster emphasis with four core placement cues; remaining families at least named.
hints: Normal; lognormal; exponential; gamma; chi-square; t; F; beta; continuous uniform.
Cues: symmetric continuous; positive skewed product/claims; waiting/memoryless; flexible positive shape family.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Continuous entry requires roster and core placement cues before calculation days.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, chi-square, t, F, beta, continuous uniform. Example cues: Normal (symmetric continuous approximation; lognormal) positive skewed magnitudes; exponential (waiting/memoryless; gamma) flexible positive continuous shapes.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Naming only Normal, or dumping formulae without placement cues.
success_criteria: Support/role cues for Normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: place and refuse Normal default
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Individual claim sizes are strictly positive and right-skewed. (1) Which continuous family (or short-listed pair) would you place first, and why? (2) Refuse Normal-by-default for this quantity in one sentence.
knowledge_checks.body: Prefer positive skewed families (lognormal/gamma); refuse Normal on support/shape grounds.
hints: Lognormal or gamma commonly fit positive skewed magnitudes.
Refuse Normal: support on all reals / light left tail vs strictly positive skew.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Continuous judgement refuses Normal theatre for positive skewed claim sizes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Start with lognormal or gamma because claim sizes are strictly positive and right-skewed. Refuse Normal-by-default because a symmetric all-real support model mismatches the support and skew of the quantity.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Default Normal 'because CLT' without addressing support/skew of the individual size.
success_criteria: Positive skewed family preferred with warrant.
Normal default refused with support/shape reason.
